title: ProbeResult
description: v2 (2026-07-29): outcome of one dry-run request through an agent's current chain — 「试跑一次」 in the agent drawer footer (spec §10.1). Answers 'is this actually working right now' without making the user start a real turn, and replaces the session-level source pinning we explicitly do not build (spec §9). Inherits the resolution-event redaction invariant: classified outcomes only, never raw upstream error bodies. NOTE the outcome field is `reachable`, not `ok`: this object is nested under the standard envelope (`{ok: true, probe: ProbeResult}`), where `ok` already means 'the API call itself succeeded'. A probe that cleanly establishes the upstream is broken is a successful API call reporting `reachable: false` — the two must not share a name.

reachable.description: Whether this source can serve a turn RIGHT NOW — request success, not transport reachability (definition corrected 07-29, review round 5). The round-4 wording was 'whether the upstream actually answered', which contradicted this file's own frozen example: a `balance_exhausted` is learned FROM a completed 402, so the upstream did answer, yet the example reports `reachable: false` and must — 「试跑一次」 asks 能不能用, and a source that answers only to refuse is not usable. An implementer following the old sentence would have emitted `reachable: true` with a required `error`, which the true branch forbids, leaving that probe with no valid representation at all. THE NAME IS RETAINED DELIBERATELY: it is load-bearing in api.md's explanation of why this field is not called `ok`, and the transport question it appears to ask is still answerable from this object without a second field — `latency_ms != null` means the attempt completed. So the two questions are separable: `reachable` = usable, `latency_ms` = completed. Never conflate either with the envelope's `ok`.

source_id.description: The source that served (or failed) the probe — the first runnable candidate in this backend's chain for the probed model. NON-NULLABLE (07-29, review round 4): returning this object already means a candidate was resolved and attempted, because the no-candidate case is the separate `probe_no_candidate` error envelope. The v1 draft made it nullable 'for defensive serialization', which only bought the right to answer 「跑不通」 without saying what was tried — the one thing a probe exists to report.

model_id.description: The model actually sent upstream, mapping applied (the resolved id, not the menu identifier the caller passed in). Non-nullable for the same reason as `source_id`.

latency_ms.description: Round trip of the minimal request. THE ONLY NULLABLE FIELD besides `error`, and deliberately so: it is the one value that depends on the attempt finishing. null means the attempt never completed — the UI renders 未完成, never 0 ms. WHICH failures completed is a total function of `error`, not an emitter judgement (07-29, review round 5): exactly two keys in the closed vocabulary are transport failures (`models.source.cooldown.network` / `.timeout`) and null is reserved for those two. Every other key — the whole needs_action family AND the response-based cooldowns (429 rate limit, cycle quota exhausted, upstream 5xx) — was learned FROM a completed upstream response, so it has a measured duration. Round 4 pinned only the needs_action half, which left a 429 free to report `latency_ms: null` and render a measured response as 未完成; the partition below closes the whole set in both directions.

error.description: i18n key when reachable=false, mirroring the source `state.detail_key` vocabulary. Never raw upstream text. A CLOSED ENUM, not a prefix pattern (07-29, review round 5): round 4 used `^models\.source\.(cooldown|needs_action)\..+` believing that enforced the redaction invariant, but `.+` accepts anything after a trusted-looking prefix — `models.source.cooldown.network: <raw upstream body>` matched it and would have carried an upstream payload into the API and the UI. A prefix check is a naming convention, not a boundary. The outcome set is finite and already enumerated (five self-healing causes, four that need the user, one unclassified), so the vocabulary is closed and a new cause is a contract change that comes here to declare its remedy. VOCABULARY HOME: `source.schema.json` → `state.detail_key` owns these keys — ALL THREE status families, cooldown + needs_action + the single `error` key it pins as a `const`; this is a mirror, because draft-07 has no cross-file `$ref` the contract test can resolve. `models.source.error.unclassified` was added here in round 7: round 6 introduced the `error` status and its key in `source.schema.json` alone, leaving a probe that hit an unmappable failure with no legal value for a REQUIRED field — the source could enter `error` but no probe could report why, and the mirror claim in this very sentence made the omission a documented self-contradiction rather than a gap. The lists must stay identical, and that is checked mechanically ACROSS files, not trusted — see the vocabulary mirror table in README.md and api.md → Serializer completeness. Explicitly null when reachable=true, so clients never distinguish absent from null.

via_mapping.description: true when a per-agent mapping rewrote the requested model id for this probe. Non-nullable (07-29, review round 4): it is known the moment a candidate resolves, so it is answerable on every object that gets returned.

allOf.$comment: v2 (07-29, review round 3): the nullability above was per-field and therefore too loose in combination — `reachable: true` with a null `source_id` and a non-null `error` validated, i.e. 'it answered, we don't know who, and here is why it didn't'. ROUND 4 moved the identity half UP to the type level: `source_id` / `model_id` / `via_mapping` are now plainly non-nullable, which is strictly stronger than pinning them in each branch and removes the branch bookkeeping entirely — a returned ProbeResult always identifies what was tested, in BOTH directions, and no future branch can reintroduce the hole. What is left here is genuinely conditional: `latency_ms` null means 'the attempt never completed', which a reachable probe contradicts by definition, so 未完成 belongs to the false branch alone.

v2 (07-29, review round 3): the converse half. `error` is the field the UI renders instead of a latency, so an unreachable probe that carries no key leaves the drawer with nothing to say — the same 'required but nullable' gap, at the other end. `latency_ms` stays nullable on this branch on purpose: an attempted failure may or may not have completed.

v2 (07-29, review round 4; made TOTAL in round 5): which failures completed is decided by the error key, not by the emitter. Round 4 pinned the needs_action family alone — every one of those is learned FROM a completed upstream response (402/401/403 telling us the balance is out, the key is revoked, the account is banned), so `latency_ms: null` there would render a completed billing answer as 未完成. But the cooldown family is MIXED, and round 4 treated it as if it were uniformly transport: `rate_limited` (429), `quota_exhausted` and `server_error` (5xx) are all completed responses too, so they were left free to report null and reproduce the exact defect one family over. The partition is by key, and only `network` / `.timeout` are transport. Listing the completed keys explicitly rather than negating the transport pair is deliberate: with a closed enum both forms are equivalent today, but an added key would silently inherit 'completed' from a negation, whereas this list forces the contract change to say which side it is on — and round 7 is that mechanism working as designed: `models.source.error.unclassified` joined the enum and had to declare a side here. It is COMPLETED. An unclassified failure is one the adapter could not map, which means something came back to be unmappable; a request that never finished is not unclassified at all, it is `network` or `timeout` by definition.

v2 (07-29, review round 5): the converse, which is what makes the partition total instead of one-directional. Round 4's shape said 'these keys require a latency' and stopped, so 未完成 remained writable for anything not named — the open half is how the 429 case survived a round whose whole purpose was closing this class. Stated from the null side there is nothing left over: a probe that never completed MUST be one of the two transport failures, because those are the only two ways an attempt can fail to finish. Any other key with a null latency is now unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. Round 5 also claimed this left 「no undefined combination in either direction」; that claim was false, and the branch below is the direction it missed.

v2 (07-29, review round 9): transport failures require a NULL latency — the half round 5 thought it had closed. Both prior branches read from one side only: 'these eight completed keys need an integer' and 'a null latency must be transport'. Neither forbids `error: models.source.cooldown.timeout` with `latency_ms: 287`, so a request that never finished could validate carrying a measured round trip, and the drawer would render 超时 next to 287ms — a completed-looking answer for the one class of failure that by definition did not complete. Stated in both directions the pair is finally a partition: transport ⇔ null, the other eight keys ⇔ integer, `reachable: true` ⇔ integer with no error. No example changes; the transport example already carries null.
